key_insight: Optimizer-state quantization for AdamW should be designed in preconditioner space, because 4-bit rounding errors in the second moment can distort the adaptive update even when the state error is small.
engineering_relevance: The paper offers a practical path to lower-memory 4-bit AdamW training that better preserves validation loss across large language model pretraining and fine-tuning.
method: ZIP-SR: keep zero in the second-moment codebook and compute stochastic-rounding probabilities in preconditioner space.
ZE-EDEN: use a zero-excluding second-moment codebook and rescale the quantized block to reduce preconditioner distortion.
Use 4-bit NF4 for the first moment, with targeted stochastic rounding of the LM-head first moment during the final 10% of training.
evidence_signal: Across GPT- and Llama-style runs from 130M to 2.7B parameters, both methods reduced the mean validation-loss gap to 32-bit AdamW versus TorchAO 4-bit AdamW, with up to a 70% gap reduction, and they also improved supervised fine-tuning results.
watch_item: The methods add extra quantization-design and calibration details, so implementation choices around codebook selection, stochastic rounding, and LM-head handling may affect reproducibility and deployment complexity.
paper_title: Rounding in Preconditioner Space: Redesigning 4-bit AdamW Optimizer-State Quantization
